top_choice_rationale: The optical lattice clock (Katori and Ye) is a demonstrated new regime of measurement, reproduced at the 10^-18 level in several laboratories and already yielding clues from nature (gravitational redshift over millimetres, limits on drifting constants and dark-matter couplings). The credit is the pair that all proposers named, and the citation rests on measured physics, not on the pending redefinition of the second. The only alternative is no award, which is worse for a mature, well-reproduced achievement that every committee member supports.
